protocols.attempts: 0 now; at most one future specifically authorized lookup, if technically needed
protocols.risk: DNS is itself an external request

protocols.rule: No generic probe, alternative endpoint, or invented health URL

protocols.attempts: 0 now; at most one future specifically authorized handshake only if documented and technically feasible without synthesis
protocols.rule: Do not send synthesis content or trigger TTS; if handshake unavoidably initiates service synthesis, stop at planning and request different approval

proposed_future_scope_not_authorized.request_budget: Strictly one permitted attempt for the separately scoped future diagnostic; no built-in library retry or fallback; if a DNS step plus handshake would count as more than one external operation, disclose each and obtain approval first

redaction.rule: Sanitize in memory before writing logs/artifacts; errors logged as class/code only

Is a legitimate documented non-synthesis endpoint or handshake method identified? If not, do not probe.
Which exact protocol and single action, if any, receives owner approval?
Are security/log redaction constraints independently reviewed?
Is Stage1 actual synthesis still separately unauthorized?
